name: softbody-pra-seam
title: Soft bodies PR-A: ISoftBodyBackend seam, SoftBodies health row and per-feature GPU failure state
issue: Approved by the user 2026-10-14: proposal C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/physx-soft-bodies.md (read it FULLY first, sections 1, 2 ('GPU status coupling (must fix in PR-A)'), 5 PR-A, 6, and 'Decisions (user, 2026-10-14)'). This item is stage PR-A ONLY (CI-verifiable, no hardware): do not implement the component, tetrahedralisation, CPU solver or any PhysX deformable-volume calls (those are PR-B and PR-C). Particles PR-C (#129) is MERGED into master: read its design (engine/include/engine/physics/IParticleBackend.hpp, the generation-counted handle helper, PbdDriver/PhysXPbdDriver, PhysXBackend.cpp GPU probe and FailParticles/PollParticleFailure, GpuStatus.hpp, Application.cpp health rows, tests/engine/physics/GpuProbeTests.cpp and the fake driver pattern) first and mirror its style. Scope: (1) a new interface engine/include/engine/physics/ISoftBodyBackend.hpp (name per the proposal) with the minimal seam the proposal specifies (create/destroy system by handle, step/update, read-back of vertex positions, name/status), reusing the SHARED generation-counted handle helper: if the particles code embeds the generation counter in IParticleBackend, factor it into a small shared header/class used by both with NO behaviour change for particles (particles tests must pass unchanged); `IPhysicsBackend::GetSoftBodyBackend()` returning nullptr by default (and for PhysXBackend until PR-C). (2) Split the GPU failure state per feature: today PR #129's `FailParticles` rewrites the single `_gpuStatus`; change it so the scene/probe status stays in `_gpuStatus` and each feature (particles, softBodies) has its OWN failure state; each health row composes scene status + its own failure, and `Physics.IsGpuAvailable` reflects the scene/probe only; a soft-body failure must never flip the Particles row and vice versa; existing behaviour of the Particles row and the existing particle failure-chain tests must remain identical (extend, do not weaken, those tests). (3) Add the `SoftBodies` health row beside Particles at Application.cpp: Disabled everywhere in CI with the detail wording the proposal gives (generic SubsystemStatus: no protocol change), and document the row. (4) Tests (all CI-verifiable, run on every leg): the shared handle helper (generation invalidates old handles even at the same address), the default null seam, the SoftBodies row is Disabled with the right detail on a CPU-only build and with physics.gpu off/auto/on when no GPU, the failure-state split (inject a particle failure through the existing InstallParticleDriverForTesting seam: the SoftBodies row is unaffected; and a fake soft-body failure hook, if you add one for the test, does not flip Particles), Lua `Physics.IsGpuAvailable` unchanged. (5) Docs: docs/physics.html (health rows, per-feature failure semantics) and docs/testing.html rows; keep the 'SoftBodies' wording consistent with the proposal. No protocol change. Nothing builds locally; CI is the build (8 checks, required `linux (Release, x86_64, Clang)`; Windows PhysX-ON legs compile PhysXBackend).
acceptance: ISoftBodyBackend seam + shared generation-counted handle helper, particles behaviour unchanged (existing particle tests pass unchanged)
Per-feature GPU failure state: a particle failure never flips the SoftBodies row and the reverse; Physics.IsGpuAvailable reflects the scene probe only
SoftBodies health row Disabled in CI; docs updated; no protocol change
notes: Reviewer: confirm the refactor of the particle failure coupling does not change particle behaviour (health row text, Physics.IsGpuAvailable, fallback to CPU), the shared handle helper keeps the generation semantics, no PhysX deformable calls leaked in, tests prove the split in both directions.
